points: Rabbi Binyamin Lau suggests the covenant here is the new one made by King Yoshiyahu, during what everyone saw as a spiritual revolution.
Yirmiyahu says: you look so observant, but inside you have gone back to the sins of your fathers. A dangerous message no one wants to hear.
The people of Anasos, his own hometown, want to kill him, and Hashem says they will be punished more than anyone. The Radak: because they were his relatives and should have protected him.
"No prophet in his hometown" is not a midrash; it comes from the Christian Bible. And Judaism believes the opposite.
We push down people we grew up with because their growth makes demands on us. Instead we should say: if they could change, so can I.
